answer: Each new agent identity must lock one distinct registered asset—say a copper token—in a public escrow account until retirement, and the registry rejects any clone that reuses that asset. The attacker pays a nonrefundable 5-copper registration fee plus the full opportunity cost of the locked token, so every extra clone adds a real loss before any reward. A shared trellis of audit records and an ivory-coded revocation flag make duplicate assets detectable, so the marginal clone is strictly negative-EV.
